To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1a) Attitudes toward schools were not related to friendship involvement but were related to popularity and to the similarity of attitudes between friends; (1b) Popularity was associated with school attitudes; (1c) The similarity of attitudes was positively related for high SES females; and (1d) Interpersonal attraction was positively related to similarity of attitudes for high SES females.

the attitudes of the individual sixth grade pupil toward school are affected by his or her own sex, social status, and the school attitudes of his or her classmates, particularly those of the most popular and attractive classmates, and the extent to which the individual is involved with friends.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the social environment of the classroom and school attitudes of sixth grade pupils.
the interpersonal conditions that influence the attitudes of sixth grade children toward school.
the interpersonal context in which school attitudes develop.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the classroom environment has a direct and indirect effect on school attitudes.
the attitudes of sixth graders are related to their interpersonal relations in the classroom, but that the relationship is complex and not easily summarized by a single statement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the classroom peer environment is an important influence on school attitudes and that the effects of the environment are mediated by the individual’s own social position.
the social environment of the classroom is an important influence on the development of school attitudes and that the social environment may be a more important influence than the teacher.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the social environment of the classroom is a powerful determinant of student attitudes toward school, and that this environment is influenced by the social status and attitudes of students in the classroom.
the relationship between friendship involvement and school attitudes is not straightforward and is mediated by other factors such as sex and socioeconomic status.
we need to think about the ways in which we can support our students in the classroom and how we can create a positive environment for learning.
